Our first task is to show that the quotient stack <MATH_0001> associated to
a ``flat and locally finitely presented groupoid'' is an algebraic stack.
See
Groupoids in Spaces,
Definition <REF_0001>
for the definition of the quotient stack.
The following lemma is preliminary and is the analogue of
Algebraic Stacks,
Lemma <REF_0002>.

Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme contained in <MATH_0002>.
Let <MATH_0003> be a groupoid in algebraic spaces over <MATH_0004>.
Assume <MATH_0005> are flat and locally of finite presentation.
Then the morphism <MATH_0006> is flat, locally of
finite presentation, and surjective.

Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme and let <MATH_0002>
be a <MATH_0003>-morphism. We have to show that the projection
<MATH_0004>
is surjective, flat, and locally of finite presentation.
We already know that the left hand side
is representable by an algebraic space <MATH_0005>, see
Algebraic Stacks, Lemmas <REF_0001> and
<REF_0002>.
Hence we have to show the corresponding morphism <MATH_0006> of
algebraic spaces is surjective, locally of finite presentation, and flat.
Since we are working with properties of morphisms of algebraic
spaces which are local on the target in the fppf topology we
may check this fppf locally on <MATH_0007>. By construction, there exists
an fppf covering <MATH_0008> of <MATH_0009> such that

Clearly the last <MATH_0019>-fibre product is represented by the algebraic

It is also surjective as <MATH_0023> has a section (namely the identity

This proves the lemma.
